entries.sense_en: the workshop where a blacksmith heats and shapes iron

synonyms.nuance: The fire or hearth itself; also used for the whole workshop, a bit more technical.
General place for making things; says nothing about metal or fire.

entries.sense_en: paved with small rounded stones

synonyms.nuance: Covered with any hard surface, such as stone, concrete or brick.
Full of stones, not deliberately laid as a road surface.

entries.sense_en: strict, plain and severe, with no comfort or pleasure

synonyms.nuance: Demanding that rules be followed; about behavior, not lifestyle.
Serious and disapproving in manner or face.
Simple and undecorated; neutral, not necessarily religious or severe.

entries.sense_en: deeply and sincerely religious

synonyms.nuance: Also shows religious devotion, but can hint at showy or self-satisfied holiness.
Plain, general word; does not say how strong the faith is.
Loyal to a belief or person, not only in religion.

entries.sense_en: dull grey in colour, like the metal lead

synonyms.nuance: Neutral colour word; leaden adds heaviness and gloom.
Lacking brightness; does not point to a heavy grey colour.

entries.sense_en: a long narrow flag carried on a knight’s lance

synonyms.nuance: A large flag, often with a family or group emblem.
Any long narrow strip that flutters, including party decorations.

entries.sense_en: a man who is very proud of his fashionable clothes and looks

synonyms.nuance: More mocking: a man silly and vain about clothes.
synonyms.example: a fop in a silk vest

synonyms.nuance: A rich man who chases pleasure and women; clothes are not the point.

entries.sense_en: a person who has sunk to immoral or corrupt habits

synonyms.nuance: Someone shameless in sin, often said half-jokingly.
Specifically a man free from moral limits in sex and pleasure.

entries.sense_en: like a lion, with a proud look and thick mane-like hair
entries.sense_ko: 사자 같은, 사자 갈기 같은 머리에 위풍당당한

synonyms.nuance: Plain, literal word; leonine is more literary and about looks.
Grand and impressive, with no link to lions.

entries.sense_en: strange because it does not fit together with its surroundings

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for one thing that does not belong in a setting.
synonyms.example: I felt out of place there.

synonyms.nuance: Two things that do not go together, e.g. clothes or socks.
Wrong for the occasion or manners, more a moral or social judgment.

entries.sense_en: lasting a long time and hard to get rid of

synonyms.nuance: Done again and again by custom or habit, not an illness.
Continuing without stopping, but may not be a long-term condition.
Never stopping; no idea of being a lasting problem.

entries.sense_en: a junior Church of England priest who helps the parish priest

synonyms.nuance: The priest in charge of a parish; higher than a curate.
General word for an ordained clergyman of any rank.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 curate(전시를 기획하다, /ˈkjʊreɪt/)와 끝소리가 다릅니다: 명사는 ‘큐어릿’.

entries.sense_en: so clearly true that it cannot be doubted

synonyms.nuance: True even when people would like to deny it.
Everyday word; less formal and less emphatic.
Beyond any question, often used of quality or authority.

entries.sense_en: unhealthily fixed on gloomy or unpleasant things

synonyms.nuance: Sad and dark in mood; not necessarily unhealthy.
Horrible because it is about death; used of things, not of a general attitude.
Plain word; morbid says the mind is drawn to disturbing things.

entries.sense_en: a room under a church, often used for burials

synonyms.nuance: Any arched underground room, e.g. a bank vault or tomb.
The grave or burial chamber itself; a crypt can be a whole room in a church.

entries.sense_en: the part of a church tower where the bells hang

synonyms.nuance: Everyday term; the whole tower, not just the bell room.
The pointed top of a church tower, not the space for bells.

entries.sense_en: speech that insults God or sacred things

synonyms.nuance: An act (not only words) that violates something holy.
synonyms.example: It is sacrilege to burn a Bible.

synonyms.nuance: Rude or swearing words, often without religious meaning today.

entries.sense_en: in a light, careless way, as if the matter were not serious

synonyms.nuance: Relaxed and unworried; neutral in tone.
Disrespectful about something that deserves seriousness.
Cheerful and confident, with a lively, easy manner.

entries.sense_en: having a lazy, drooping way of standing or walking

synonyms.nuance: Bending forward, often from age or to reach something.
Shoulders pulled up and forward, from cold, fear or work.

entries.sense_en: living a wild life of drink and pleasure with no moral limits

synonyms.nuance: Stronger: damaged by heavy drinking and sex.
Any wrong behavior; dissolute is about wasting oneself on pleasure.
Everyday and mild; can even sound fun.

entries.sense_en: like a friendly, playful uncle

synonyms.nuance: Warm and cheerful with anyone; not tied to an uncle’s role.
Protective and caring like a father, more serious than avuncular.

entries.sense_en: a person who lives very simply and denies himself pleasures for religion

synonyms.nuance: Lives alone away from society; asceticism is about self-denial, not loneliness.
Member of a religious community with vows; not always extreme.

entries.sense_en: of a bluish-grey, deathly pale colour

synonyms.nuance: Pale, as from illness, without the blue-grey tint.
Grey-white, like ashes, often from shock.

entries.modern: In modern speech “livid” usually means “very angry”: “She was livid.”
entries.tip_ko: 요즘 영어에서는 주로 ‘몹시 화난’의 뜻으로 쓰입니다.

entries.sense_en: quickness in acting; readiness to act at once

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for being on time or quick.
Speed that may be careless or hurried.

entries.sense_en: rough and low in voice, as when the throat is sore or upset

synonyms.nuance: Low and rough, often in a pleasant or attractive way.
Informal; a frog-like voice from a cold.

entries.sense_en: dead, ruined or finished

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; ends an activity or a career, not necessarily a life.
Certain to fail or die soon; about the future, not the present.
Completely over, said of plans or of a person.
synonyms.example: The idea is dead and buried.

entries.sense_en: to support a statement with further evidence

synonyms.nuance: General: say something is true; needs no separate evidence.
Informal; support someone’s story or a claim.
synonyms.example: My friend backed up my story.

synonyms.nuance: Check and prove that something is true, usually by testing.

entries.sense_en: to form a judgment about something before knowing all the facts

synonyms.nuance: Assume something is true without proof; not always negative.
Informal: decide too fast from few facts.

entries.sense_en: to declare in court that someone is not guilty

synonyms.nuance: Everyday: remove blame, in court or otherwise.
Show or say someone was not to blame, often after evidence appears.
Officially forgive a person found guilty; unlike acquit, it assumes guilt.

entries.sense_en: in a stubborn way, refusing to change one’s mind

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; can be mild or even admiring.
Harder and colder: unmoved by pity or argument.
Like a mule: silly, sulky stubbornness.

entries.sense_en: seeming evil or threatening

synonyms.nuance: Openly threatening; suggests danger coming right now.
Warning of bad things to come; about signs, not people.
Actually bad; sinister only seems bad or hides something.

entries.sense_en: eager to give orders or advice nobody asked for

synonyms.nuance: Interfering in other people’s private business.
Informal: likes ordering people around.
Held by authority; a neutral word that looks similar.

entries.sense_en: will not be believed or accepted as an excuse

synonyms.nuance: Informal US: an idea or excuse that will not be accepted.
Says the argument has logical holes.

entries.sense_en: grand and impressive, commanding respect

synonyms.nuance: Beautiful and grand in a powerful way, often of scenery.
Calm and self-respecting; less grand.
High in character or birth; moral or class sense.

entries.tip_ko: 달 이름 August(/ˈɔɡəst/)와 강세가 다릅니다: 형용사는 뒤에 강세.

entries.sense_en: an unbeliever; someone who rejects the speaker’s religion

synonyms.nuance: Neutral description of someone without faith.
Old word for non-Christians; often scornful.
Someone who believes there is no God; a chosen position, not an insult.

entries.sense_en: proof that you were somewhere else when a crime happened

synonyms.nuance: Any reason given to avoid blame; not proof of being elsewhere.
A made-up account to hide the truth.

entries.sense_en: slow, heavy and serious in manner

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for weight or mood; less about slowness.
Done with obvious effort; stiff rather than natural.
Serious and dignified, without the dull, plodding sense.

entries.sense_en: a person with no belief in the speaker’s (Christian) religion

synonyms.nuance: Follower of an old nature or many-gods religion; more neutral, historical.
Unbeliever seen from within a specific faith; also strongly hostile.
synonyms.example: a crusader’s word for an infidel

entries.sense_en: to show any sign of fear or surprise
entries.sense_ko: 눈 하나 깜짝하다(주로 부정문: 눈 하나 깜짝 안 하다)

synonyms.nuance: US version of the same idea: show no reaction.
A quick physical jerk of fear or pain.

entries.modern: “without turning a hair” → “without batting an eye” (US)
entries.tip_ko: 보통 never/without과 함께 ‘전혀 동요하지 않다’는 뜻으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: nervous, restless and overexcited, as if feverish

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; can mean a real fever or fierce excitement.
Wild with worry or hurry.
Unable to stay still; calmer than febrile.

entries.sense_en: a wooden frame used to hang criminals; here, death by hanging

synonyms.nuance: The loop of rope itself, not the frame.
The raised platform for executions; also used for building sites.

entries.tip_ko: 복수형 모양이지만 단수 취급하는 경우가 많습니다.

entries.sense_en: to publicly accuse someone of a crime or wrong

synonyms.nuance: Say that someone did wrong; need not be public or formal.
Strongly say something is wrong, often in moral terms.
Tell the authorities; neutral and without anger.
synonyms.example: report a crime to the police

entries.sense_en: a sudden violent fit of anger, madness or pain

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, short word for a sudden attack or outburst.
A sudden release of strong feeling in words or action.
Medical: a sudden attack, e.g. of epilepsy.

entries.sense_en: to put forward an idea or theory for others to consider

synonyms.nuance: More general: suggest a plan, idea or marriage.
Everyday phrasal form of propound.
Offer an argument or idea in a formal, careful way.

entries.sense_en: to be logical and stand up to a test or challenge

synonyms.nuance: Survives checking; often used in the question ‘Does it stand up?’
Everyday and weaker: seems reasonable.
Formal: an argument built without mistakes.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 부정문·의문문에서 ‘(주장이) 말이 안 된다’는 뜻으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: in a bad-tempered, complaining way over small things

synonyms.nuance: Easily annoyed; more general and not always complaining.
Childishly sulky, like a spoiled person.
Informal: in a low, bad mood, often from tiredness.

entries.sense_en: to laugh in a quiet, mean way at someone

synonyms.nuance: Silly, light laughter, often nervous or innocent.
Quiet, warm laugh to oneself.
Open scorn shown by the face or words, not by laughing.

entries.sense_en: (past tense smote) to strike or destroy with great force, especially as divine punishment

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for hit; smite is Biblical or literary.
Kill or destroy with a sudden blow, often by fate or God.

entries.sense_en: keeping one’s thoughts and knowledge to oneself

synonyms.nuance: Shy and unshowy about feelings, mainly a personality trait.
Hiding things on purpose, often suspiciously.
Refusing to say anything about a topic.

entries.sense_en: so vast that no limit can be seen

synonyms.nuance: Common, often positive word for having no limit.
Plain and common; no upper limit.
Strictly without end; also mathematical.

entries.sense_en: a state where everything is upside down and confused

synonyms.nuance: Total disorder with no sense; topsy-turvy is reversal.
A big sudden change or disturbance.

entries.sense_en: a large waterfall or violent rush of water

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; cataract is large, powerful and poetic.
A fast, strong stream of water, or of words or feelings.

entries.sense_en: arrogantly giving orders, as if one ruled others

synonyms.nuance: Always trying to control other people.
Forcing one’s views on others in a heavy, annoying way.
Belonging to an emperor or empire; a different, neutral meaning.

entries.sense_en: walking in a proud, showy way, as if important

synonyms.nuance: Bold, rolling walk that shows confidence or insolence.
Walk to be seen, or show something off in public.
Long, purposeful steps; not necessarily proud.

entries.sense_en: to jump back or turn away suddenly in fear or disgust

synonyms.nuance: A small, quick body movement from pain or fear.
Draw back slowly out of fear or shyness.
Pull back from fear or embarrassment; often humble.

entries.sense_en: a person of very low intelligence (now an offensive word)

synonyms.nuance: Common insult for a foolish person; now used casually.
Someone who acts unwisely; milder and not about mental ability.
synonyms.example: I was a fool to trust him.

entries.modern: “imbecile” → “person with an intellectual disability” (medical, avoid as an insult)
